articles.title: Persistent Latent Memory for Multi-Hop LLM Agents: How a 6G Handover Paper Closes the Agent Cold-Start
articles.reason: The article introduces a practical method for reducing tokenization overhead in multi-agent LLM pipelines, directly relevant to building efficient agentic workflows for enterprise clients.
articles.summary: This article explains Inductive Latent Context Persistence (ILCP), a technique for passing compressed hidden states between LLM agents to avoid redundant context reconstruction and reduce token usage. The approach is highly relevant for optimizing multi-hop agent pipelines, such as those built with LangGraph or similar frameworks. While not finance- or insurance-specific, the method can be immediately evaluated for improving latency and cost in production RAG or agentic systems.
